subject: Prompt & response retention: deletion SLA and subprocessor onboarding
messages:
From: Ava Richardson <ava.richardson@healthly.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Healthly.ai Procurement <procurement@healthly.ai>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on data use (retention, subprocessors, ownership)

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the product demo last week — Healthly.ai is excited about Redwood's low-latency routing. Before we proceed to signature, our legal and privacy team asked for clarifications on a few items in the DPA you shared:

1) Model improvement opt-out: can you commit that Healthly.ai data (prompts + generated responses) will not be used to further train or fine-tune Redwood models or third-party models? We need an operational guarantee and evidence of enforcement.

2) Prompt/response ownership: we require explicit language confirming that prompts and model outputs are the customer's IP and that Redwood will not assert ownership or derivative rights beyond delivering the service.

3) Retention & deletion SLA: for audit reasons we need a deletion SLA for inference logs and ephemeral caches. Target ask is configurable retention (default 30 days), with an option for 0-7 days for high-security customers. Can Redwood provide controls and a formal deletion certificate on request?

4) Subprocessors & onboarding: our procurement team needs a current subprocessor inventory and a short description of any planned changes (particularly KMS providers and cross-border infra). We also need to know the notice window for new subprocessors and whether Healthly.ai can object.

We attached a redline of the draft DPA and a small spreadsheet of the subprocessors we discovered from your public page — please confirm and advise next steps.

Appreciate a short reply with concrete operational options (e.g., config knobs, attestation pack, timeline) and whether any of this will require legal redlines.

Best,
Ava
Ava Richardson
Head of Legal Operations, Healthly.ai

Attachments: DPA-HealthlyAI-redline-v3.docx (docx, 72KB); subprocessor_inventory_20270522.csv (csv, 9KB)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Richardson <ava.richardson@healthly.ai>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on data use (retention, subprocessors, ownership)

Hi Ava — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then an internal ask below.

1) Model improvement opt-out: yes — we can offer a contractual "no model training" commitment for Healthly.ai production traffic. Operationally we implement this by routing your tenant to a non-training serving pool and ensuring telemetry is excluded from model-training pipelines. We can provide a signed attestation and an ops-runbook excerpt for audit.

2) Prompt/response ownership: we are comfortable with language that explicitly states customers retain ownership of prompts and outputs. By default Redwood retains derived telemetry (e.g., anonymized latency/quality metrics) but will not assert derivative IP over customer prompts/responses. We can incorporate explicit wording in Section 4.2 of the DPA.

3) Retention & deletion SLA: we offer configurable retention windows. Standard hosted tiers default to 30 days; for enterprise Dedicated/Private we can enable a 7-day or 0-day retention option. Deletion is executed via automated sweep + overwrite of ephemeral KV caches; for on-demand legal deletion requests we can provide a signed deletion certificate within 5 business days.

4) Subprocessors & onboarding: current subprocessors (infra, KMS, monitoring) are listed in the attached CSV. We provide 30 days' notice for material changes to subprocessors; customers can raise objections and, in limited cases, we support on-prem/private deployment to avoid specific subprocessors.

Next steps: Olga and David — can your teams prepare the attestation pack (SOC2 excerpt + ops runbook snippet), confirm the exact clause language for the DPA redline, and confirm whether the 7-day retention option requires additional engineering work or a configuration toggle?

Ava — happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Thanks,
Rafael
VP, Partnerships & Sales | Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA-HealthlyAI-redline-v3.docx (docx, 72KB)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Questions on data use (retention, subprocessors, ownership)

Hi team — forwarding Healthly's asks and Rafael's summary. Quick notes from Legal/Privacy perspective: 

- Attestation pack: Legal can assemble a SOC2 excerpt, current subprocessor inventory, and an ops runbook excerpt that describes the non-training serving pool and telemetry exclusion. I estimate a ~3 business day turnaround for a sanitized pack suitable for procurement.

- DPA language: prefer to add a short, explicit paragraph under "Customer Data / Model Use" that: (a) commits to no training/fine-tuning on customer inference data; (b) confirms customer ownership of prompts/outputs; (c) describes telemetry we retain (aggregated/anonymized performance metrics only). I'll draft suggested language and attach to the redline.

- Retention SLA: Engineering — is the 7-day retention an opt-in flag we can flip for a tenant in hosted, or will that require a Dedicated/private seat? If it's a runtime toggle we should document the risk matrix (e.g., prefix caching vs full-kv eviction cost). Also need to confirm deletion certificate flow (audit logs + deletion job runbook).

David — can you confirm estimated eng effort to expose a 7-day/0-day retention toggle and to produce an automated deletion certificate? If effort > 3 days we'll need to propose a timeline to Healthly.

Olga
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference

--- Forwarded attachment: DPA-HealthlyAI-redline-v3.docx (docx)

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Ava Richardson <ava.richardson@healthly.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on data use (retention, subprocessors, ownership)

Hi all — quick update from engineering after a short scoping pass.

- 7-day retention toggle: feasible as a per-tenant configuration in hosted. Implementation is small (we already have a retention param); we need to expose it in the admin console and add a short verification job. Estimated effort: ~2 engineer-days + QA.

- 0-day (no-storage) mode: possible but requires an internal opt-out path that bypasses some aggregations. Estimate: ~6-8 engineer-days and an operational review (we need to validate telemetry fallbacks and alerting). Recommend we reserve 0-day for Dedicated/Private or a signed compliance SOW.

- Deletion certificate: we can produce a signed deletion certificate that includes job id, timestamp, and affected keys. Automation for generating certificates on-demand: ~3 engineer-days. We can deliver a manual certificate within 5 business days for initial requests.

- Subprocessors: CSV looks accurate. KMS provider is currently KeyCloud (US-east) for hosted; Dedicated customers can choose on-prem KMS or a region-specific KMS via our private deployment options.

Rafael — happy to join a call with Healthly to walk through the retention switches and show the ops runbook.

Thanks,
David
Director, Product Engineering | Redwood Inference
